A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSFS system. Their main text, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 report original experiments on API parsing, semantic retrieval, rollback, keyword retrieval and file sharing.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including accuracy, retrieval metrics, execution times and file-sharing success rates.

M1.justification: v1 Section 4.4 specifies comma-separated parameter extraction followed by regex processing. v2 introduces per-API JSON schemas and structured JSON parsing, but still describes comma-separated outputs. This inconsistency leaves unclear whether the parser procedure changed or its documentation was expanded. The detailed syscall and API procedures otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same API-parsing, semantic-retrieval, rollback, keyword-retrieval and file-sharing tasks. The paper-file examples and single-condition/multiple-condition retrieval scenarios are retained; no new evaluated dataset, domain or task coverage is established.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparators: Gemini-1.5-flash and GPT-4o-mini without LSFS for semantic retrieval; search window, TFS-grep and TFS-grep* for keyword retrieval; and Gemini, GPT-4o-mini, AutoGPT and Code Interpreter for sharing. Parser backbones also remain unchanged. Baseline descriptions move to Appendix E.

E3.justification: Both retain 30 examples per API, retrieval conditions with 10/20/40 files, 20 sharing prompts, the same metrics and the rollback sweep extending to 40 versions. Prompt and preprocessing descriptions match after relocation. Naming the default parser backbone supplies previously missing information without establishing a changed evaluation setting.

E4.justification: The rollback scalability analysis and semantic-retrieval case study are retained; the latter moves from Section 5.2 to Appendix F. File-sharing failure examples and Algorithms 1–3 move from Appendix D to Appendix G. No new ablation, robustness experiment or case-study evidence is added.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The retained counts of API examples and sharing prompts describe test cases rather than repeated runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes Gemini-1.5-flash LSFS retrieval times for 20 and 40 files from 116.69 and 123.86 seconds to 16.69 and 23.86 seconds. These revisions agree with the unchanged 92.2% and 92.4% reductions. Accuracy entries, Tables 3–4 and the parser and rollback plots retain their results; no rerun is documented.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results, proofs or mathematical derivations. The retained appendix pseudocode illustrates file-sharing procedures; v2's architectural design discussion adds no formal theory.

C1.justification: v2 replaces broad abstract claims with specific claims of at least 15% retrieval-accuracy improvement, 2.1× retrieval speed, over 89% keyword-retrieval F1 and 100% rollback/sharing success. The introduction similarly sharpens the performance claims. The central contribution of semantic indexing, reusable interfaces and natural-language file management remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds modularity, efficiency and fault-tolerance design rationales, and attributes the exclusion of Gemma-2 and Qwen-2 from semantic retrieval to unstable performance. It removes the specific independent-version-storage explanation for stable rollback time. Existing text-file, security and extensibility limitations are mostly condensed into Section 6.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies all-MiniLM-L6-v2 as the embedding model and GPT-4o-mini as the default parser backbone. It expands schema-related parser documentation and corrects syscall names in Table 1. LlamaIndex was already disclosed in v1 Appendix A; detailed APIs and prompts are retained after relocation, and the code URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations on JSON schemas and structured formats, Sentence-BERT, Mobile-Agent/Mobile-Agent-v2 and AppAgent, while removing several general reasoning and AIOS-background references. It more explicitly positions LSFS as file-management infrastructure supporting agents. The underlying relationship to earlier semantic file systems and parsers remains similar.

P1.justification: The revision substantially reorganizes the exposition: API details, baseline descriptions and the retrieval case study move into appendices, while appendix future directions move into the conclusion. The abstract, introduction, architecture and parser discussions are rewritten, and an appendix roadmap is added. Title, author list, headings and citation style also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced by a detailed retrieval pipeline; Figures 2–3 revise interface labels and add API-schema elements. Table 1 revises its rows and syscall names, prompt tables are reformatted, and the retrieval case-study figure moves to the appendix. The document adopts a different layout. Figure 1's caption and surrounding panel references still describe the old illustration.

improvement.justification: Naming the embedding model and default parser backbone improves reproducibility, and correcting Table 2 resolves two numerical inconsistencies. Reorganized implementation details also aid navigation. These are limited gains with essentially unchanged empirical validation; the conflicting JSON/comma-separated parser descriptions and stale Figure 1 caption weaken the clarity improvements.
